newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana rejoices at choice of Annan to head U.N..
newsitem.headline: Ghana rejoices at choice of Annan to head U.N..

text.p: Ghanaian newspapers rejoiced on Saturday at the choice of Ghanaian diplomat Kofi Annan as United Nations secretary-general while the head of the Organisation of African Unity said the decision was a victory for Africa.

Ghana's state-owned Daily Graphic and and the Ghanaian Times hailed Annan's choice as a double victory for Ghana, coming hard on the heels of the re-election of President Jerry Rawlings in polls that monitors called exemplary for Africa.
"This has to be the greatest week in the history of the Republic of Ghana," commented the Graphic in an editorial titled "Ghana's historic double victory".

The soft-spoken 58-year-old Annan, undersecretary-general for peace-keeping operations, won the support of all 15 Security Council members on Friday after France dropped a veto threat. The choice now goes to the 185-nation General Assembly, which will appoint him on Tuesday.

The secretary-general of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), Salim Ahmed Salim of Tanzania, said the choice was also a victory for the OAU, which wanted an African after Washington opposed Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali for a second term.

"I am confident that given your vast experience and commitment, you will be able to live up to the enormous challenges and responsibilities that face you as secretary-general," Salim said in a message sent to Annan.

Salim was also seen as a potential candidate for the post of U.N. secretary-general but he was never nominated after President Nelson Mandela said France had threatened to veto him because he speaks no French.
Newspapers in Ivory Coast reported on Saturday that Ivorian Foreign Minister Amara Essy, one of three Africans who vied with Annan, withdrew his candidacy before the final polling.
They said Essy, who had been second to Annan in earlier voting, acted in the interest of keeping the job in Africa.
But Le Republicain, one of the Ivory Coast's opposition dailies, accusing President Henri Konan Bedie of not doing enough to back his foreign minister, said Essy had gone out with his head high.

"It appears that if this election had followed the fundamental principle -- one country one vote -- the candidate of Ivory Coast, which counts numerous friends in the world, would have been the most favoured," Le Republicain said in an editorial written before Annan's triumph.
"Alas we have to contend with the law of those who really govern our planet earth."
Ghana's Graphic said Annan, who will become the first black African to head the world body, had an "awesome" task ahead.

"Arguably he is assuming the second most important office in the world, probably second in stature only to the President of the United States. The duties of that office must be awesome in any situation. But it is particularly so now, given the new challenges facing the world," the Graphic added.
